component.name: SpectroScope
component.summary: Spectrum analyzer for multiple SDR platforms

description.p: SpectroScope is a Rust/egui rewrite of QSpectrumAnalyzer: a spectrum analyzer and waterfall display for software-defined radio hardware. The waterfall is rendered on the GPU, so a long sweep history stays scrollable and smooth instead of being redrawn on the CPU frame by frame.

ul.li: Live spectrum, persistence, peak hold and a GPU waterfall
Built-in rtl_tcp backend that needs no external helper program
Backends for soapy_power, hackrf_sweep, rtl_power, rtl_power_fftw and rx_power
Recording of sweeps and ImageJ-compatible TIFF or PNG export
Band plans for a long list of countries, plus the QO-100 transponder

description.p: In this sandboxed build the rtl_tcp and demo backends work out of the box; rtl_tcp is the supported way to reach real hardware, by running the rtl_tcp server on the host or on another machine. The backends that drive an external sweep program (soapy_power, hackrf_sweep, rtl_power, rtl_power_fftw, rx_power) need those programs installed outside the sandbox, where SpectroScope cannot start them; use the AppImage or a native package if you depend on them.
